name: sgs/post-grid
title: SGS Post Grid
description: Display posts in grid, list, masonry, or carousel layouts with AJAX filtering and pagination.

grid.label: Grid
grid._layer_note: Block root and grid/list/masonry/carousel track combined. layer_detect.py's MF-3 guard makes the root OUTER regardless of its own display:grid.
grid._note: No `display`/`align-items`/`order`/`overflow` attribute exists on this block — honest GAPs.
grid._note_animation: FR-35-6 — the scroll-reveal preset (sgsAnimation/sgsAnimationDuration/sgsAnimationEasing) resolves via explicit attrMap (no `prefix` declared, per ROLLOUT REQUIREMENT 1). This block has NO staggerDelay attribute, so anim:stagger is an honest gap; anim:parallax/anim:trigger are also honest gaps (no bgParallax/scroll-trigger attrs).

card.label: Post card

hover._noBaseByDesignNote: css:transform (scaleHover) legitimately has NO resting counterpart: a card's resting scale is 1 by definition, so a 'resting scale' control would be clutter rather than capability. Bean-ruled 2026-08-20. NOT a suppression hatch — css:box-shadow was ALSO hover-only on this element and was fixed by BUILDING the resting control (shadow/shadowColour), not by adding it here. Use only where the resting value is genuinely implicit.

card._note: cardStyle (card/flat/overlay/minimal) is a preset, not a Layout-cluster control; no static border/padding/radius attrs exist for the card — background/shadow are client-overridable (cardBgColour/shadow+shadowColour), the rest hover-only (backgroundColourHover/borderColourHover/shadowHover), same shape as sgs/card-grid's card-tile gap. scaleHover is declared here (css:transform on the card element's :hover) so the generator seeds it css_property='transform' / css_element='card' / css_state='hover' — fixing the derived-classifier smell (was 'background-color,transform' / css_state NULL) at SOURCE (R-31-1 declarative channel) and giving the per-element state-lift a clean row to route the draft's `.sgs-post-grid__card:hover{transform:scale(N)}` onto. shadowHover added to this attrMap 2026-08-16 (shadow-architecture migration off the preset-only picker, matching sgs/card-grid's card-tile 'css:box-shadow':'shadowHover' hover mapping) — shadowHoverColour (the sibling colour attr) is classified via scripts/attr-classification-overrides.json, same pattern as the other shadow-colour companion attrs (D621/D622). shadow/shadowColour added 2026-08-20 to close a STATE_WITHOUT_BASE conformance gap (client could style shadowHover but had no resting shadow attribute) — mirrors the hover pair exactly, on the BASE attrMap rather than a state. An unset shadow is an honest gap: style.css's `--sgs-card-shadow` custom property keeps its existing hardcoded default (the cardStyle preset's look), and render.php only emits an inline override of that same property when shadow is non-empty, so the preset is unchanged until the client sets a value. shadowColour is the companion colour attr, same pattern as shadowHoverColour.

image.label: Post image
image._note: Renamed from 'card-image' 2026-08-15 to match the DB's own css_element spelling for imageZoomHover (transform) - the audit script does exact-string matching, so the near-miss was real drift, not a false positive. aspectRatio/imageSize/showImage/imageZoomHover govern this element; no supports.sgs.imageControls declared on this block (unlike gallery/hero/feature-grid), and no Text/Fill/Layout style attrs exist for it.

title.label: Post title
title._note: css:color resolves via the default convention (titleColour). No font-size/weight attrs exist — honest GAPs.

excerpt.label: Post excerpt
excerpt._note: css:color resolves via the default convention (excerptColour). excerptLength is a content-length control, not a style member.

meta.label: Meta (date/author)
meta._note: css:color resolves via the default convention (metaColour).

category-badge.label: Category badge
category-badge._note: css:color resolves via the default convention (categoryBadgeColour).

read-more.label: Read more link
read-more._note: css:color resolves via the default convention (readMoreColour). readMoreText is content, not style.

inner.label: Scroll track
inner._note: The scroll/grid track (.sgs-post-grid__inner, render.php line 331) - the element that actually scrolls in carousel mode and carries the real grid-template-columns (render.php line 509-536), distinct from the 'grid' (root) element above. columns is claimed via explicit attrMap rather than declaring 'layout' in clusters: a first draft used clusters:["layout"] with layer:"GRID", which reached the SAME bare (no-prefix) arrangement members the 'grid' element also reaches (both bare-prefix, both layer OUTER/GRID) and produced 3 CONTESTED findings - including 'order', which on this block is the WP_Query sort-order attribute (asc/desc), nothing to do with CSS order, a coincidental bare-name collision this element's clusters declaration would otherwise have manufactured. clusters:[] + explicit attrMap avoids all of it while still claiming columns cleanly. Found live 2026-08-15: DB tagged 1 attr css_element='inner', undeclared until now.

fx._comment_providesNatively: Spec 38 FR-38-13 / §7. This block owns drag-to-scroll through its OWN inspector toggle, which targets the DESCENDANT element that actually scrolls. The generic 'Scroll & effects' picker stamps data-sgs-fx onto the block ROOT, which is not the scroller here — so offering `draggable` there too would give the client TWO controls for ONE capability, and the picker's one would silently do nothing. Declaring it here removes the dud picker entry via generate-fx-qualifying-blocks.py without removing the capability, exactly as sgs/responsive-logo does for `draw`. Ruled 2026-07-31 after the roster derivation surfaced it on five blocks at once (gallery had it latently already). NOTE sgs/timeline deliberately does NOT carry this: its scroller IS the block root, so the picker lands correctly there.
